summary: mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count 0 for every query on a private repo while gh search returns results — a silent wrong-answer, not an error
description: On cbartens/bkit (PRIVATE), mcp__github__search_issues returns {total_count:0} for every query including the control `repo:cbartens/bkit is:issue is:open`, despite 39 matching issues. `gh search issues --repo cbartens/bkit worktree` and `gh api search/issues` (total_count 39) both succeed with the same account. Impact: bkit-design Step 3.1 (related-issues search) specifies this MCP tool and its own rule says `0 hits -> None.`, so the workflow records `None.` and proceeds — silently dropping related-issue context from every design on a private repo. Failure is silent (clean 0, no error), so the `on call error -> Search unavailable.` branch never fires.
rootCause: Not yet root-caused. Candidates: GitHub search API requires different token scope/visibility handling for PRIVATE repos than the REST issue endpoints the MCP server uses elsewhere (issue_read/list_issues work fine); or the MCP server drops the owner/repo scoping params. Note gh (keyring classic token) succeeds where the MCP server (GH_TOKEN fine-grained PAT) returns 0 — consistent with the known GH_TOKEN scope gap.
remediation: Two parts. (1) bkit workflow: Step 3.1 must not treat 0 hits as authoritative — distinguish `search unavailable` from `genuinely no hits` (e.g. probe with a control query, or require the mapped gh fallback per #341 6b/6c). (2) #341 design input: this is direct evidence that 6i (trackers stay on MCP) has a SILENT-failure hole — the gh->MCP fallback rule (6b) covers gh-outage but nothing covers MCP-returns-garbage. The design should add a rule that MCP tracker reads which can silently return empty are either verified or mapped to a gh fallback.

summary: bkit-status-fold.test.ts hashed via macOS-only `md5`, passing locally but failing on Linux CI
description: Sub-plan 1's T1.3 test .bkit/src/bkit-status-fold.test.ts:68 computed the BKIT_STATUS_FOLD blob md5 by shelling out to `sh -c '...' | md5`. `md5` is the BSD/macOS binary; Linux (GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest) ships `md5sum` instead, so the pipe errored 'Command failed'. The test passed on the macOS dev box across every local `pnpm test` run this build and only surfaced when CI ran the workflow_dispatch lane (run 29486640718, bkit-tests-unit). Local-only green is exactly the class docs/testing.md and feedback_verify_install_and_upgrade_live warn about. All other lanes (integration, static) passed; bkit-tests-check failed only as a downstream consequence of the unit lane.
rootCause: Portability: shell-out to a BSD-only command (`md5`) with no Linux fallback, in a test that only ever ran on macOS locally before CI.
remediation: Hash in-process with node:crypto createHash('md5').update(out).digest('hex') — platform-independent, no shell-out. Verified all three (Node crypto, macOS md5, MEASURED_MD5) agree at ed1c4a236d35499f39033206d5b75480. Fixed on feat/58-workflow-counters before merge.

summary: poll_dispatch() sets GH_ALL_ERRORED=false inside a command-substitution subshell — the assignment never reaches the caller, so GH_ALL_ERRORED stays 'true' even when gh succeeded
description: The pre-#341 inline CI-Dispatch Gate kernel (bkit-build.md close-workflow, bkit-debug.md PR-mode + LOCAL-mode) calls its poll function as `R=$(poll_dispatch)` to capture the echoed found/none/err result. `$(...)` forks a subshell, so poll_dispatch's own `GH_ALL_ERRORED="false"` assignment (made on a successful gh call) is scoped to that subshell and discarded on return — the caller's GH_ALL_ERRORED never flips from its initial 'true'. Downstream, `if [ "$GH_ALL_ERRORED" = "true" ]` (the post-kernel unresolved(gh-error) branch) can misclassify a run where gh worked fine but genuinely found no CI check as gh-error instead of no-ci/timeout-dirty/autoroute-mismatch. Discovered while extracting this logic into bkit_wait_ci (tests/bkit-runtime.bats row 5) — a bats assertion on ALLERR=false after a successful zero-result poll failed until fixed.
rootCause: Command-substitution subshell scoping: variable writes inside $(fn) never propagate to the parent shell.
remediation: Fixed in the #341 extraction: bkit_wait_ci (.bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/bkit-runtime.sh) derives CI_WAIT_ALL_ERRORED from the poll's echoed result ([ "$_bwc_r" != "err" ] && CI_WAIT_ALL_ERRORED="false") in the CALLING shell, after the substitution returns, instead of inside the subshelled poll function. The inline poll_dispatch()/GH_ALL_ERRORED duplicates in bkit-build.md/bkit-debug.md are being replaced by calls to the fixed bkit_wait_ci in the same change.
